rules.title: Ensure 'Minimum password length' is set to '14 or more character(s)'
rules.description: Short passwords are prone to brute-force and dictionary attacks. A length of at least 14 characters dramatically increases computational attack costs.
rules.remediation: Set Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Account Policies > Password Policy > Minimum password length to 14.

rules.title: Ensure 'Account lockout threshold' is set to '5 or fewer invalid logon attempt(s)'
rules.description: Without an account lockout threshold, an attacker can attempt infinite password guesses against interactive and network logon portals.
rules.remediation: Configure Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Account Policies > Account Lockout Policy > Account lockout threshold to 5 or fewer attempts (not 0).

rules.title: Ensure 'User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode' is set to 'Enabled'
rules.description: If EnableLUA is disabled, UAC is completely turned off and all administrative processes run with full unfettered token privileges, allowing zero-click root compromise.

rules.title: Ensure 'User Account Control: Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation' is set to 'Enabled'
rules.description: The secure desktop prevents malicious code from forging mouse or keyboard clicks to silently elevate permissions without user knowledge.

rules.title: Ensure 'User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators' is configured properly
rules.description: If set to 0 (Elevate without prompting), administrative tasks silently execute with full token privileges without notifying the user.
rules.remediation: Set HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin to 2 (Prompt for consent on the secure desktop) or 5.

rules.title: Ensure 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' is set to 'Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM'
rules.description: Legacy LM and NTLMv1 protocols use broken single-DES encryption and can be cracked or relayed in seconds using automated open-source tools.

rules.title: Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Domain: Firewall state' is set to 'On'
rules.description: Disabling the Domain firewall profile exposes the machine to lateral movement from any compromised host on the domain network.

rules.title: Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Private: Firewall state' is set to 'On'
rules.description: Disabling the Private firewall profile exposes host ports to local network scanning and unauthorized connections.

rules.title: Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Public: Firewall state' is set to 'On'
rules.description: Disabling the Public firewall profile leaves the endpoint completely undefended when connected to untrusted public Wi-Fi networks.

rules.title: Ensure 'Turn off Windows Defender Antivirus' is set to 'Disabled' / Real-time Protection is 'On'
rules.description: Real-time protection monitors file system activity and process execution to block malicious code before execution.

rules.title: Ensure Defender Exclusions do not contain broad folder, process, or extension rules
rules.description: Path exclusions (e.g. C:\, Temp folders, Downloads) or process exclusions allow malware to execute without antivirus inspection.
rules.remediation: Audit and remove broad exclusions with Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionPath <path>.

rules.title: Ensure 'Tamper Protection' is enabled
rules.description: Tamper Protection prevents malicious software and unprivileged admin processes from disabling Defender through registry modifications or PowerShell.
rules.remediation: Enable Tamper Protection in Windows Security Settings or via Microsoft Intune.

rules.title: Ensure 'Require user authentication for remote connections by using Network Level Authentication' is set to 'Enabled'
rules.description: NLA requires clients to authenticate before an RDP session is established, mitigating pre-authentication exploits like BlueKeep (CVE-2019-0708).

rules.title: Ensure 'Secure Boot' is enabled and UEFI mode is active
rules.description: Secure Boot prevents rootkits and unauthorized bootloaders from executing prior to the Windows kernel initialization.
rules.remediation: Enable Secure Boot in UEFI firmware configuration.

rules.title: Ensure 'Audit Credential Validation' / 'Logon' is set to 'Success and Failure'
rules.description: Auditing logon successes and failures is mandatory for identifying brute-force attacks and detecting unauthorized lateral movement.
